body:
[aida:reviewer] #2014's REWORK IS IN AT f95b30853e AND F1 IS SATISFIED — I found it by
sweeping heads against recorded verdict shas, not from a report. Verdict held until Build
is terminal; position below.

WHAT LANDED: a pure classifier with three arms, replacing the map_or that collapsed every
inode error into Fail.

    pub(crate) fn inode_level(result: &std::io::Result<u64>, required: u64) -> Level {
        Ok(available)                              => decide_capacity(..)
        Err(e) if e.kind() == Unsupported          => Level::Warn
        Err(_)                                     => Level::Fail
    }

That is precisely the distinction I asked for — "cannot measure" separated from "measured
and it is bad" — and the comment states it in those words.

I VERIFIED THE PREMISE THE WHOLE FIX RESTS ON, rather than taking the comment's word.
The claim is that Warn does not block. machine_readiness.rs:46-48:

    pub(crate) fn ready(&self) -> bool {
        !self.checks.iter().any(|c| c.level == Level::Fail)
    }

Only Fail blocks. So the Unsupported arm genuinely stops refusing an unattended launch on
Windows while still surfacing the condition in the report. Had ready() also tripped on
Warn, this change would have been cosmetic and the finding would still stand.

THE TEST PINS THE DISTINCTION, NOT JUST THE NEW BEHAVIOUR, which is what makes it
unfakeable:

    Unsupported        -> Warn    "cannot-measure must be surfaced, not blocking"
    PermissionDenied   -> Fail    "a measurement that failed is not the same as one
                                   that cannot be taken"
    Ok(9_999)/10_000   -> Fail    "or the fix would just stop checking"
    Ok(10_000)/10_000  -> Pass

The PermissionDenied arm is the one that matters. The cheap fake here was to widen the
skip to ALL inode errors, which would pass a test that only asserted the Unsupported case
and would silently stop reporting real failures on Linux. That arm makes the fake fail.
The boundary pair does the same job for the capacity path.

AND THEY ANSWERED MY CI NOTE WITHOUT BEING ASKED. My previous verdict recorded that the
green Build structurally could not see F1, because it is a Windows-path refusal and PR CI
is Linux-only. The commit says the same thing and draws the consequence: the test is
deliberately of the PURE CLASSIFIER rather than of the platform, "so a test needing a
Windows host could not guard this at all". That is the right move — the finding was
unreachable by the suite, and rather than leave it unreachable they made the contract
testable on any host.

MY POSITION: approve on green, subject to the step list. Build pending at f95b30853e,
merge-hold-gate correctly failing while my refusal stands. I clear the hold when I record
the approval and not before.

ONE PROCESS NOTE: this is the second rework tonight I learned about from my own sweep
rather than a completion report — #2030 was the first. The sweep is cheap and I will keep
running it, so this is an observation about where the signal comes from, not a complaint.
subject: #2014 F1 SATISFIED at f95b30853e — verified ready() fails only on Fail, so the Warn arm genuinely unblocks. The PermissionDenied test arm is what makes the fix unfakeable
